library_preparation_preflight.summary: Artifact and all transitive deps (openai-java-core, okhttp, micrometer, azure-identity, spring-context-support) resolve directly from Maven Central — no custom repo, extra dependency, Docker image, or env var needed. Sibling module spring-ai-autoconfigure-model-openai already depends on spring-ai-openai as testImplementation and its (passing) tests never make a real OpenAI call; they only exercise property binding and the Options/builder classes that live in org.springframework.ai.openai. The standard generated scaffold (testImplementation on spring-ai-openai + assertj-core) matches every sibling spring-ai test project and is sufficient.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Mirror the spring-ai-autoconfigure-model-openai test's approach: exercise OpenAiChatOptions/OpenAiEmbeddingOptions/OpenAiImageOptions/OpenAiAudioSpeechOptions/OpenAiAudioTranscriptionOptions/OpenAiModerationOptions builders and Model class construction/configuration directly. Pass a placeholder API key string (e.g. "test-key") when constructing models/clients — the library takes it as a plain argument, not from an env var — and avoid invoking methods that perform real OpenAI HTTP calls (call/stream/image/audio/moderation requests), since no API credentials or network egress exist in this test environment.
risks: Restricting coverage to Options/builder construction (no live calls) likely leaves the deeper request/response record classes and the underlying openai-java-core SDK call path under-exercised; this repo has no WireMock/MockWebServer/Testcontainers pattern for OpenAI-like API clients to close that gap, so it's an accepted limitation shared with the sibling autoconfigure module rather than something to introduce here.
